audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings does not reflect the post-anchor financing cost reset
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.875 million annual gross coupon increase; H1 2026 net interest expense increased $4.2 million year over year; $184.2 million of net note proceeds remained after redemption before subsequent uses
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor retains the former financing cost, while the bridge includes June 2026 cash that may include incremental borrowing proceeds.
audit_findings.evidence: The increased principal and extended maturity of the 2034 Senior Notes will also increase the amount of interest we will be required to pay in 2026 and beyond.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch. Replacing $300 million of 5.75% notes with $500 million of 5.625% notes raises annual gross coupon expense from $17.25 million to $28.125 million, equal to 4.5% of the $240.1 million OE anchor. The $184.2 million retained proceeds equal 4.9% of base equity value. The combined OE and bridge exposure is large enough to move estimated value materially, although the record does not establish how much of the proceeds remained in June cash.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate normalized after-tax OE using the 2034-note coupon, term-loan swaps, hedge reclassifications and recurring financing costs; trace the $184.2 million retained proceeds through acquisitions, repurchases and other uses; then rerun all scenarios with only non-borrowed excess cash added.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-dependent growth may be credited without its required investment
audit_findings.magnitude: $51.5 million invested in 2025, equal to 21.4% of anchor OE; $47.7 million invested in H1 2026, equal to 19.9% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired revenue can enter the growth assumptions even though acquisition consideration is excluded from projected OE and acquired-intangible amortization is added back.
audit_findings.evidence: We continued to diversify our operations through our acquisition strategy by investing $51.5 million during the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is unresolved rather than a demonstrated valuation error because the record does not separate organic and acquired growth. It is nevertheless material: recurring acquisition spending has recently approached one-fifth of annual anchor OE, and the 2025 acquisitions were expected to contribute $53.3 million of annual revenue. Crediting that contribution without its recurring investment requirement could materially overstate distributable earnings and compounded value.
audit_findings.action: Build an organic-growth bridge for each scenario, identify acquired revenue embedded in the 3% and 6% paths, and rerun any acquisition-dependent scenario after charging the normalized acquisition investment needed to produce that growth.

audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor and latest balance-sheet bridge use different business perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: $52.6 million total 2026 acquisition consideration through June, 1.4% of base equity value; acquired H1 revenue was $12.0 million and acquired net loss was $0.5 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The June bridge reflects acquisition cash outflows and acquired assets and liabilities, while FY2025 OE excludes the acquired operations.
audit_findings.evidence: Between December 31, 2025 and the filing of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, we completed three acquisitions for total combined consideration of approximately $28.7 million, the largest of which is Thermo-Tech Mechanical Insulation, Inc. for total consideration of approximately $19.5 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but the filed scale does not support a material effect on this valuation. The acquired businesses generated only 0.8% of H1 consolidated revenue, and pro forma H1 net income was $99.3 million versus $99.7 million reported. The direction is mixed because omitting acquired earnings can understate value, while the disclosed acquired losses can overstate it. The measured amounts are too small relative to $3,768 million of base equity value to change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Use the filed pro forma acquisition results to estimate same-perimeter OE and rerun the bridge once, confirming that consideration is reflected only through reduced cash and is not deducted again.

audit_findings.title: The scenarios may skip a documented near-term cyclical decline
audit_findings.magnitude: H1 2026 revenue decreased 0.5%, installation same-branch sales decreased 4.5%, residential same-branch sales decreased 8.5%, operating income decreased $18.6 million and net income decreased $14.7 million year over year
audit_findings.mechanism: Starting every scenario at nonnegative growth may overstate first-stage OE and the earnings base from which later growth compounds.
audit_findings.evidence: Housing starts are forecasted to decrease in 2026, as Fannie Mae predicts 1.31 million starts for an overall decrease of 3.7% compared to 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The near-term weakness is now demonstrated by filed H1 results, not merely forecast. However, revenue and net-income declines do not establish the corresponding full-year OE decline, and the record cannot determine whether the weakness is temporary or persists into later forecast years. The valuation effect is therefore unquantified and materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Compute H1 and trailing-twelve-month 2026 OE on the valuation's existing definition, separate organic volume, pricing and margin effects, and rerun scenarios with an explicit 2026 contraction followed by the existing recovery assumptions.

audit_findings.title: Large self-insured claims reserves could be understated
audit_findings.magnitude: $79.9 million gross workers' compensation, general-liability and auto reserves at June 2026; $64.1 million net after $15.8 million of recoverables; any reserve deficiency is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adverse reserve development would reduce future OE through additional claims expense and cash payments; an unrecorded deficiency would also leave an equity claim outside the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The assumptions underlying the ultimate costs of existing claim losses are subject to a high degree of unpredictability, which can affect the liability recorded for such claims.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest liabilities are available and do not demonstrate under-reserving: net specified reserves were $64.1 million at June 2026 versus $64.0 million at December 2025. Nevertheless, the filed reserves equal 26.7% of anchor OE and depend on highly unpredictable actuarial assumptions. Because no adverse-development sensitivity or claims triangle is supplied, the possibility remains open but its materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 actuarial reports and loss-development triangles, reconcile paid claims and recoverables by coverage, quantify reasonable adverse-development sensitivities, and rerun OE for any required reserve strengthening.

audit_findings.title: A contingent multiemployer pension claim may sit ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: A triggered withdrawal liability would create a cash claim ahead of common equity that is separate from ordinary pension contributions already included in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: If a participating employer chooses to stop participating in these multiemployer plans, the employer may be required to pay those plans a withdrawal liability based upon the underfunded status of the plan.
audit_findings.explanation: No withdrawal, probable exit or recorded withdrawal liability is identified. Fewer than 3% of employees are union represented, the plans are not individually significant, and 2025 pension contributions were $3.0 million, but those facts do not bound a statutory withdrawal claim. This is therefore a forward-looking contingency to monitor rather than a demonstrated current valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current plan funding notices and employer withdrawal-liability estimates, and reopen the valuation only if an exit, restructuring, distressed co-employer or other triggering event becomes probable.
